2607.25648.title: Why Public Service AI Governance Frameworks Risk Failing in the Age of General-Purpose AI: Lessons from Policing
2607.25648.paper_summary: Public services face growing pressure to adopt artificial intelligence (AI) to close the gap between rising demand and falling resources. That pressure has intensified with general-purpose AI (GPAI): AI built on large language models that can be directed by prompt alone to perform an effectively unbounded range of tasks. We argue that the properties that make these models attractive - their generality, accessibility, and low deployment cost - undermine the conditions under which AI safety has historically been pursued. The safety concepts that public service governance frameworks foreground - accuracy, bias, explainability, and accountability - were made tractable by narrow, purpose-built AI, and the mitigations that guidance documents prescribe presuppose exactly what GPAI removes. Accuracy cannot be quantified over unbounded outputs. Bias cannot be disaggregated when outputs are free-text judgements rather than categorical predictions. Explainability gives way to the appearance of explanation, and accountability erodes as outputs are optimized to persuade. We develop this through the case of policing, where the consequences of governance failure are most severe, and show why the same failure is likely to recur across other public services. The two mitigations that dominate policing AI strategy - expert evaluation and human-in-the-loop oversight - both rest on assumptions that GPAI violates. Safety assurance thus shifts from an intrinsic feature of building an AI tool to an optional add-on. We recommend a clear taxonomic distinction between narrow and general-purpose AI in governance documentation, a preference for technological parsimony, a pause on operational deployment of GPAI in policing until adequate evidence exists, and a coordinated national safety infrastructure with the authority to generate that evidence and determine when responsible deployment is achievable.
2607.25648.paper_summary_zh: 公共服務面臨越來越大的壓力，要求採用人工智慧（AI）以縮小日益增長的需求與資源減少之間的差距。隨著通用人工智慧（GPAI）的出現，這種壓力變得更加劇烈：GPAI是基於大型語言模型構建的AI，只需通過提示即可執行實質上無限制範圍的任務。我們認為，使這些模型具有吸引力的特性——它們的通用性、可及性和低部署成本——削弱了歷史上追求AI安全的條件。公共服務治理框架所突出的安全概念——準確性、偏見、可解釋性和問責制——是由狹隘的、專門構建的AI所使其可行，而指導文件所規定的緩解措施則預設了GPAI所移除的內容。準確性無法在無界限的輸出上量化。當輸出是自由文本判斷而非類別預測時，偏見無法被分解。可解釋性讓位於解釋的表象，而隨著輸出被優化以說服，問責制也逐漸侵蝕。我們通過警務案例來發展這一點，在這裡，治理失敗的後果最為嚴重，並展示為何同樣的失敗可能會在其他公共服務中重演。主導警務AI策略的兩種緩解措施——專家評估和人類參與監督——都基於GPAI所違反的假設。因此，安全保證的重心從構建AI工具的內在特徵轉變為可選的附加功能。我們建議在治理文件中明確區分狹隘和通用AI，偏好技術簡約，暫停在警務中操作性部署GPAI，直到有足夠的證據存在，並建立一個具備產生該證據的權威和決定何時能夠負責任部署的協調國家安全基礎設施。
2607.25648.author: Sam Relins et.al.
